3: # TiffCraft
4: 
5: TiffCraft is a header-only C++20 library for reading uncompressed TIFF images.
6: It provides a customizable image-data export interface and requires no separate
7: library binary.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Usage
21: 
22: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
23: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
24: the following:
25: 
26: ```C++
27: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
28: #include <functional>
29: 
30: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
31:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
32:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
33:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter));
34:   auto image = tiffExporter.takeImage();
35: 
36:   // your own image processing code
37: 
38:   return 0;
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
43:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
44: format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
45: image.
46: 
47: TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed by copying the headers into
48: your project. No build step required: no compiled artifact, no link step, and
49: no CMake needed (CMake-based consumption is documented separately).
50: 
51: # Which headers do you need?
52: 
53: TiffCraft is header-only; copy the headers from `include/tiffcraft/` into
54: your project and include them directly. No CMake required (CMake-based
55: consumption is documented separately).
56: 
57: When copying the headers, keep them together in one directory; if the folder
58: is renamed, update the consumer-facing `#include <tiffcraft/...>` paths in
59: your own code accordingly.
60: 
61: - `TiffImage.hpp`: core TIFF reading; self-contained.
62: - `TiffExporter.hpp`: flat-buffer pixel decoding; requires `TiffImage.hpp`.
63: - `TiffStdOut.hpp`: metadata output/printing; requires `TiffImage.hpp`.
64: - `TiffCraft.hpp`: umbrella header; includes everything.
65: 
66: `TiffImage.hpp` is self-contained; the other headers depend on it by filename
67: (e.g. `#include "TiffImage.hpp"`), which resolves relative to the including
68: header's own directory, so they can live together in any folder. The
69: `tiffcraft/` folder name applies only to consumer-facing include paths (e.g.
70: `#include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>`), which are in the user's own code and
71: must be updated if the folder is renamed.
72: 
73: # Advanced usage
74: 
75: Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
76: to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:
77: 
78: ```C++
79: #include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
80: #include <iostream>
81: 
82: int main() {
83:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
84:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
85:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
86:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
87:       std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
88:                 << " entries." << std::endl;
89:       std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;
90: 
91:       // Add your own image processing code here
92: 
93:     });
94: 
95:   return 0;
96: }
97: ```
98: 
99: # Features
100: 
101: TiffCraft supports the following features:
102: 
103: - Reading TIFF images
104:   - Read and display image metadata
105:   - Bilevel, grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images
106:     - Varying number of bits per sample
107:     - RGB images are supported only for 3-channel images (no extra samples)
108: - Compression is NOT supported yet.
109: - Writing TIFF images is NOT supported yet.
110: 
111: Advanced users could use TiffCraft for other configurations than those
112: enumerated above by writing their customizing any of the existing exporter
113: classes, or writing their own from scratch.
114: 
115: # CMake consumption
116: 
117: ## FetchContent
118: 
119: TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed directly from its git
120: repository with CMake's `FetchContent` module:
121: 
122: ```cmake
123: include(FetchContent)
124: 
125: FetchContent_Declare(
126:   TiffCraft
127:   GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft.git
128:   GIT_TAG <release tag>   # e.g. the latest release tag
129: )
130: FetchContent_MakeAvailable(TiffCraft)
131: 
132: target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
133: ```
134: 
135: When consumed this way, the `TIFFCRAFT_BUILD_ALL` option defaults to `OFF`,
136: so the library's tests, apps, and examples are not built. The same applies
137: when consuming via `add_subdirectory` from a local checkout.
138: 
139: ## find_package
140: 
141: To consume a CMake-installed TiffCraft package:
142: 
143: ```sh
144: cmake --install /path/to/tiffcraft/build/gcc-linux-release --prefix /path/to/install
145: ```
146: 
147: ```cmake
148: find_package(TiffCraft REQUIRED)
149: 
150: target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
151: ```
152: 
153: The installed package provides the `TiffCraft::TiffCraft` namespaced target and
154: the public headers under `include/tiffcraft`.
155:

14: ## [0.2.0-Unreleased]
15: 
16: ### Added
17: 
18: - Code examples
19: - README now documents which headers are needed and the copy-only
20:   consumption path (header-only; copy the headers into the project, no build
21:   step required).
22: - CMake consumption improvements: added the `TiffCraft::TiffCraft` namespaced
23:   alias, an installable/exportable target with generated
24:   `TiffCraftConfig.cmake`/`TiffCraftConfigVersion.cmake` (for `find_package`),
25:   and a `TIFFCRAFT_BUILD_ALL` option that defaults to `ON` when building
26:   TiffCraft standalone and to `OFF` when consumed via `FetchContent` or
27:   `add_subdirectory`.
28: - Version-consistency test between the CMake `PROJECT_VERSION` and the header
29:   version constants (`TiffCraft::version()`), failing with both values named on
30:   mismatch.
31: - YCbCr (PI=6) test coverage: added the TIFF 6.0 `tests/YCBCR_SUPPORT.md`
32:   specification reference, 17 generated YCbCr test images under
33:   `tests/ycbcr_images/`, and the corresponding `ycbcr-*.ppm` ground-truth
34:   reference images (child issue of the YCbCr support effort, #38).
35: 
36: ### Changed
37: 
38: - CMake project version bumped to `0.2.0` to match the header version
39:   constants and the `[0.2.0-Unreleased]` changelog section.
40: 
41: ### Fixed
42: 
43: - `TiffExporter.hpp` no longer includes the umbrella header `TiffCraft.hpp`;
44:   it now includes `TiffImage.hpp` directly, resolving the include cycle and
45:   making the exporter header standalone.
46: - ODR violations in headers: `inline` on `version()`, `readAt()`, `writeAt()`,
47:   and both `load()` overloads (`TiffImage.hpp`); the six `operator<<` overloads
48:   moved into `namespace TiffCraft` and marked `inline` (`TiffStdOut.hpp`).
49:   Note: the stream operators are no longer visible in the global namespace;
50:   they are found via ADL, which applies to all TiffCraft types.
51: - Crash/hang fixes for malformed TIFF input: ASCII entry with count 0 no
52:   longer reads out of bounds (throws `std::runtime_error`); RATIONAL/SRATIONAL
53:   entries with a zero denominator no longer divide by zero (throws
54:   `std::runtime_error`); cyclic IFD offsets are detected and rejected (throws
55:   `std::runtime_error`).
56: - `readAt()` now detects short reads and throws `std::runtime_error`, so
57:   truncated strips/tiles no longer silently yield zero-filled buffers.
58: - `takeImage()` no longer copies instead of moving; it moves the image buffer
59:   out of the exporter, leaving it empty.
60: - `TiffExporterAny` now resets its multi-IFD state per IFD; each IFD is
61:   exported and the last successfully exported image wins (previously later
62:   IFDs were silently skipped).
63: - Example `tiff_image` reads `ImageWidth`/`ImageLength` type-agnostically, so
64:   LONG-typed entries no longer throw.
65: - README quick-start snippet fixed (removed undeclared `loadParams` argument;
66:   fixed `iffExporter` typo).
67: - `Type::BYTE` entries print as integers instead of raw characters.
68: 
69: ## [0.1.0]
70: 
71: ### Added
72: 
73: - Initial TiffCraft code for loading TIFF images and exporter for bilevel,
74:   grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images. Compression is not supported.
75: - Example `tiff_exporter` program to convert TIFF images to PNG 8-bit format.
76: 
77: ### Changed
78: 
79: - Moved all headers to `include/tiffcraft`.

3: # TiffCraft
4: 
5: TiffCraft is a header-only C++20 library for reading uncompressed TIFF images.
6: It provides a customizable image-data export interface and requires no separate
7: library binary.
8: 
9: # Objectives
10: 
11: TiffCraft is designed based on the following principles:
12: 
13: - Permissive license: to be used in open source and proprietary software.
14: - C++ header-only: to easy integration onto existing projects.
15: - Flexible but simple API: for ease of use.
16: - Feature complete: to cover a wide variety of use cases.
17:   - TiffCraft is NOT feature complete at this time! The objective is for guiding
18:     on-going development.
19: 
20: # Usage
21: 
22: For quick access to TIFF image pixel data with individual pixels aligned to
23: word boundaries (i.e. 8 bits, 16 bits, or 32 bits), you could use code like
24: the following:
25: 
26: ```C++
27: #include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>
28: #include <functional>
29: 
30: int main(int argc, char* argv[]) {
31:   if (argc < 2) { return 1; }
32:   TiffCraft::TiffExporterAny tiffExporter;
33:   TiffCraft::load(argv[1], std::ref(tiffExporter));
34:   auto image = tiffExporter.takeImage();
35: 
36:   // your own image processing code
37: 
38:   return 0;
39: }
40: ```
41: 
42: TiffExporterAny will decode and convert pixels to a flat-buffer (i.e.
43:  `std::vector<std::byte>`) with 1, 2, or 4 bytes per sample the source pixel
44: format. For example, an image with 2-bits per sample is exported as an 8-bit
45: image.
46: 
47: TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed by copying the headers into
48: your project. No build step required: no compiled artifact, no link step, and
49: no CMake needed (CMake-based consumption is documented separately).
50: 
51: # Which headers do you need?
52: 
53: TiffCraft is header-only; copy the headers from `include/tiffcraft/` into
54: your project and include them directly. No CMake required (CMake-based
55: consumption is documented separately).
56: 
57: When copying the headers, keep them together in one directory; if the folder
58: is renamed, update the consumer-facing `#include <tiffcraft/...>` paths in
59: your own code accordingly.
60: 
61: - `TiffImage.hpp`: core TIFF reading; self-contained.
62: - `TiffExporter.hpp`: flat-buffer pixel decoding; requires `TiffImage.hpp`.
63: - `TiffStdOut.hpp`: metadata output/printing; requires `TiffImage.hpp`.
64: - `TiffCraft.hpp`: umbrella header; includes everything.
65: 
66: `TiffImage.hpp` is self-contained; the other headers depend on it by filename
67: (e.g. `#include "TiffImage.hpp"`), which resolves relative to the including
68: header's own directory, so they can live together in any folder. The
69: `tiffcraft/` folder name applies only to consumer-facing include paths (e.g.
70: `#include <tiffcraft/TiffExporter.hpp>`), which are in the user's own code and
71: must be updated if the folder is renamed.
72: 
73: # Advanced usage
74: 
75: Users that prefer to decode and handle the image pixel data themselves, or need
76: to handle multiple frames per image, could write their own handler:
77: 
78: ```C++
79: #include <tiffcraft/TiffImage.hpp>
80: #include <iostream>
81: 
82: int main() {
83:   TiffCraft::load("image.tiff",
84:     [](const TiffCraft::TiffImage::Header& header,
85:         const TiffCraft::TiffImage::IFD& ifd,
86:         TiffCraft::TiffImage::ImageData imageData) {
87:       std::cout << "Loaded IFD with " << ifd.entries().size()
88:                 << " entries." << std::endl;
89:       std::cout << "Image data size: " << imageData.size() << std::endl;
90: 
91:       // Add your own image processing code here
92: 
93:     });
94: 
95:   return 0;
96: }
97: ```
98: 
99: # Features
100: 
101: TiffCraft supports the following features:
102: 
103: - Reading TIFF images
104:   - Read and display image metadata
105:   - Bilevel, grayscale, palette-color, and RGB images
106:     - Varying number of bits per sample
107:     - RGB images are supported only for 3-channel images (no extra samples)
108: - Compression is NOT supported yet.
109: - Writing TIFF images is NOT supported yet.
110: 
111: Advanced users could use TiffCraft for other configurations than those
112: enumerated above by writing their customizing any of the existing exporter
113: classes, or writing their own from scratch.
114: 
115: # CMake consumption
116: 
117: ## FetchContent
118: 
119: TiffCraft is header-only and can be consumed directly from its git
120: repository with CMake's `FetchContent` module:
121: 
122: ```cmake
123: include(FetchContent)
124: 
125: FetchContent_Declare(
126:   TiffCraft
127:   GIT_REPOSITORY https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft.git
128:   GIT_TAG <release tag>   # e.g. the latest release tag
129: )
130: FetchContent_MakeAvailable(TiffCraft)
131: 
132: target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
133: ```
134: 
135: When consumed this way, the `TIFFCRAFT_BUILD_ALL` option defaults to `OFF`,
136: so the library's tests, apps, and examples are not built. The same applies
137: when consuming via `add_subdirectory` from a local checkout.
138: 
139: ## find_package
140: 
141: To consume a CMake-installed TiffCraft package:
142: 
143: ```sh
144: cmake --install /path/to/tiffcraft/build/gcc-linux-release --prefix /path/to/install
145: ```
146: 
147: ```cmake
148: find_package(TiffCraft REQUIRED)
149: 
150: target_link_libraries(my_app PRIVATE TiffCraft::TiffCraft)
151: ```
152: 
153: The installed package provides the `TiffCraft::TiffCraft` namespaced target and
154: the public headers under `include/tiffcraft`.
155: 
156: # Feedback
157: 
158: Feedback is welcomed! Please don't hesitate to reach out by opening a
159: [GitHub issue](https://github.com/danielm5/tiffcraft/issues/new/choose)
160: if you have suggestions, feature requests, or bug reports.

## 2) Change hypothesis

Add a new CLI app `apps/tiff_info.cpp` and register it in `apps/CMakeLists.txt` exactly like `tiff_exporter`. All required output primitives already exist:
- Header/byte-order/IFD-offset/host-order summary: `os << header` (`operator<<(Header)`) — covers the default-mode header requirement verbatim.
- Full entry dump: `os << ifd` (`operator<<(IFD)`) prints an entry count followed by each entry in `Tag: …; Type: …; Count: …: Value: …` form.
- Per-IFD metadata fields: no high-level getters exist — must be read from `ifd.getEntry(Tag::…)` / `ifd.entries()` with type-agnostic value extraction (`Entry::values<uint16_t/T>()` or the `TiffExporter::getInt` helpers).
- Version: `TiffCraft::version()` (returns `"0.2.0"`) from `TiffImage.hpp`.
- Total image data bytes: sum `vec.size()` over the `ImageData` supplied to the `load()` callback (the pattern used in `examples/tiff_image.cpp`), or sum `StripByteCounts`/`TileByteCounts` entries without reading pixel data.

Two viable implementation routes:

*Route A (simple, mirrors `examples/tiff_image.cpp`):* call `TiffCraft::load(filename, callback)`. In the callback `operator()(const Header&, const IFD&, ImageData)`, use the stream operators and compute bytes from `imageData`. Limitation: `load()` (TiffImage.hpp L766–774) throws `"Unsupported IFD format"` when an IFD has neither `StripOffsets` nor `TileByteCounts`, and `readImageStrips/Tiles` throw on missing/mismatched entries or invalid offsets — so an "info" tool built this way cannot describe every parseable TIFF.

*Route B (more robust for a metadata tool):* use `TiffImage image = TiffImage::read(filename)`, then `os << image.header()` and loop `image.ifds()`. Use `os << ifd` for `--tags`; compute strip/tile info and total bytes purely from `ifd.entries()` (sum `StripByteCounts` or `TileByteCounts` values), optionally using `image.stream()` with the public static `TiffImage::readImageStrips(image.stream(), ifd)` / `readImageTiles(...)` when actual data sizes are desired. This avoids the "Unsupported IFD format" path entirely and still uses the required stream operators.

No header/library changes are needed; only a new `.cpp` and two CMake lines.

Recommended type-agnostic reader (mirrors `examples/tiff_image.cpp` L57–64; avoids including `TiffExporter.hpp`):
```cpp
auto readU32 = [](const TiffImage::IFD& ifd, Tag tag) -> uint32_t {
  const auto& e = ifd.getEntry(tag);
  switch (e.type()) {
    case Type::SHORT: return e.values<uint16_t>()[0];
    case Type::LONG:  return e.values<uint32_t>()[0];
    default: throw std::runtime_error("Unsupported entry type for " + toString(tag));
  }
};
```

- `toString(Tag)` (L42–86) → known tags as exact names, e.g. `"ImageWidth"`, `"PhotometricInterpretation"`; unknown → `std::snprintf("0x%04X", static_cast<uint16_t>(tag))`, e.g. `"0x00FE"`. Returns `std::string`.
- `toString(Type)` (L88–104) → `"BYTE"`, `"ASCII"`, `"SHORT"`, `"LONG"`, `"RATIONAL"`, `"SBYTE"`, `"UNDEFINED"`, `"SSHORT"`, `"SLONG"`, `"SRATIONAL"`, `"FLOAT"`, `"DOUBLE"`, unknown `"!UNKNOWN"`. Returns `std::string_view`.
- `operator<<(Header)` (L114–120):
  ```

   - Byte Order: Little Endian|Big Endian
   - First IFD Offset: <uint32_t>
   - Equals Host Byte Order: Yes|No
  ```
- `operator<<(Entry)` (L122–186):
  ```
  Tag: <toString(tag)>; Type: <toString(type)>; Count: <count>: Value: <v0> <v1> …
  ```
  + trailing `\n`; ASCII prints `" " + std::string(values(), bytes()-1)`; RATIONAL prints `num/den`; UNDEFINED prints ` 0xNN` in hex with width 2; loop breaks after the 7th value, appending `" ..."`.
- `operator<<(IFD)` (L188–203):
  ```
  TIFF IFD:
    Entry count: <N>
     0# Tag: …; Type: …; Count: …: Value: …
     1# …
  ```
  (`std::setw(4) << i++ << "# " << entry.second` — the entries are the `Entry` values from `std::map<Tag, Entry>`). Saves/restores stream flags via local `AutoRestore`.
- `operator<<(TiffImage)` (L205–221):
  ```
  TIFF IMAGE START -----------------------
  <Header block>
  IFD count: <N>
   0) <IFD block>
  …
  TIFF IMAGE END -------------------------
  ```
- All six operators live in `namespace TiffCraft` and are `inline`; ADL applies. No global-namespace operators exist (CHANGELOG L46–50).

### 3e) CLI nuance for `--tags`
`os << ifd` already emits the entry count and every entry, but prefixes each line with `   0# `. If the issue's wording requires bare `Tag: Type: Count: Value` lines with no prefix, print the count yourself and stream each entry directly:
```cpp
std::cout << "  Entry count: " << ifd.entries().size() << "\n";
for (const auto& [tag, entry] : ifd.entries()) std::cout << entry; // operator<<(Entry)
```
Both approaches use the required `TiffStdOut.hpp` operators; the first is the natural one-shot verbatim dump.
